parole.significato: amanat (a hostage from a local tribe taken by Russian troops during reconnaissance or exploration, e.g. in Siberia duri…
parole.testo: Via a Turkic language from Arabic أَمَانَة (ʔamāna, “surety”).
Borrowed from Turkic, from Arabic بَزّ (bazz), see more there.

parole.significato: shackles, manacles, gyves, fetters, irons (paired wrist or ankle restraints)
parole.testo: Borrowed via Turkic from Arabic قَيْدَان (qaydān), dual form of قَيْد (qayd).
Via Turkic from Arabic مَهْزُولَات f pl (mahzūlāt, “refuse, waste”), feminine plural of مَهْزُول (mahzūl). Influenced by ма́зать (mázatʹ).
From a Turkic language (compare Turkish meydan (“square”)), ultimately from Persian and Arabic مَيْدَان (maydān). The extended meanings are from Ukrainian майда́н (majdán).
From a Turkic language (compare Kazakh мешіт (mešit), Tatar мәчет (mäçet), Turkmen metjit), ultimately from Arabic مَسْجِد (masjid).

parole.significato: muezzin (the man who issues the call to prayer)
parole.testo: Via a Turkic source, from Arabic مُؤَذِّن (muʔaḏḏin, “one who calls (to prayer), crier”).
Via a Turkic source (compare Bashkir хаж (xaj), Turkish hac), from Arabic حَجّ (ḥajj).

parole.significato: dressing gown, bathrobe (for men or women)
parole.testo: A Turkic borrowing. Compare Ottoman Turkish خلعت (hilat, “kaftan”), Azerbaijani xələt (“dressing gown”), Uzbek xalat (“robe”). Ultimately from Arabic خِلْعَة (ḵilʕa, “robe of honor”).
